title: RegisterApplication
description: The body of an administrative client registration, derived from identity_application::applications::RegisterApplication. Registering an application is an ADMINISTRATIVE act, which is the whole reason every command in this module takes an actor: an application whose redirect URIs you can change is an application you can steal a code with.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; RegisterApplicationCommand has no body and no route serves it

actor_id.description: The administrator registering it. REQUIRED: a command that mutates a registration and does not name an actor has no way to be authorized. A non-administrator actor is a Forbidden refusal.
actor_id.x-test: identity_application::applications::tests::every_application_command_names_its_actor asserts actor_id is present on the serialised input

client_id.description: The PUBLIC client_id. GENERATED BY THE SERVER when absent — which is the common case, and the reason it is Option rather than String. A duplicate client_id is a domain refusal, not a silently suffixed one.
client_id.x-serde-note: Option<String> with no skip_serializing_if, so the key is always present on the wire.

access_mode.description: Which access mode. oidc receives identity claims and delegates authentication here; oauth2 is for machine-to-machine clients with no user to authenticate.

redirect_uris.description: The redirect URIs to register. Each must be absolute and fragment-free; the domain model refuses the rest. Pre-registered, never learned at request time.
redirect_uris.note: The Vec is required by the struct and may legitimately be empty at registration — Application::new builds an application with no redirect URIs yet — but a client that registers none and then tries to start a flow will be refused at the authorization endpoint.

allowed_scopes.description: The scopes to register. Pre-registered; a request outside this set is refused.

confidential.description: Register a confidential client, one that will present a secret. A public client (false) has no secret at all, which is why the secret in the response is Option and a public client is `is_confidential: false` BY DEFINITION rather than by failure. A confidential client is a server; a public client is a browser or a native app, and the latter cannot keep a secret no matter how carefully it is written.

x-response: RegisterApplicationOutcome — { application: ApplicationView, client_secret: string | null }. For a confidential client the secret is returned EXACTLY ONCE, here, and is never persisted in cleartext and never appears in any later read. The only way to obtain another is a rotation. Phase 4's exit condition makes 'a client_secret shown exactly once and never persisted in cleartext' a gate, not a preference.

x-refusals.bad-redirect-uri: ApplicationError::Domain — not absolute, or carrying a fragment, or over the bound

x-phase: Phase 4 — OIDC provider for the registration itself; Phase 5 — Applications, grants, and the self-service surface for the console screen that calls it
